title: [D4 Rendering] Closed, versioned host attribute set from fixed configuration
summary: `helena/hosts/` is the third versioned package: `__init__.py` holds the loader, the configuration reader and the host-section renderer, and `v1.py` holds the frozen closed field set, which is `address` and `device_type` and nothing else because those are the two `concept/04` names. `config/hosts.toml` is the fixed configuration and the only source triage's host knowledge has — the package imports nothing else in `helena` and no database driver, so there is no expression inside it that could evaluate to an assessment, a proposal or an enrichment row.
assumption_validated: That `concept/04`'s 'fixed configuration only' can be made a structural property rather than a convention, and can be demonstrated. It can, three ways, and all three are live: the package's imports are a closed permitted set (mutation-checked — adding `import psycopg` fails it); nothing outside the package names `HostAttributes`, `HostAttributeSet` or the private minting functions (mutation-checked — an import of `HostAttributes` into `agents.py` fails it); and with a real ThreatFox claim about the rendered host sitting in a migrated engine, whose free-form tags read `workstation` and `desktop`, the rendering still says `device_type: unknown` and carries none of the row's values. What is NOT demonstrated is that a two-field set is enough for triage to reason with — that is what `concept/04` names, not what a corpus showed.
makes_buildable: The renderer (task 28) has part one of the five-part projection finished and can call `hosts.load(...).attributes_for(address)` and `hosts.render(attributes)` for the host section's body, with `evidence_ids=()` and no `Truncation` — the host section is the one part whose size does not depend on what the host did. It also has the shape for the other four: a closed field set with a version of its own, written into the body because `RenderedSection` is frozen. D5 storage has `hosts.version(identifier)` as the replay path for a rendering that recorded an attribute set version.

verification.detail: 911 passed in 365 s (was 880 before this task; 31 new tests in tests/test_hosts.py). One of the new tests is an integration test against a migrated schema on a throwaway in-memory RisingWave: it INSERTs a real-shaped ThreatFox row for the rendered host, reads the claim back out of `helena_reference_evidence` and asserts the row is there before asserting the rendering ignores it, so it cannot pass for the wrong reason. Two structural tests were mutation-checked and both failed under mutation: `import psycopg` added to `helena/hosts/__init__.py`, and `from helena.hosts import HostAttributes` added to `helena/agents.py`. `uv lock --check` and `python -m compileall src tests scripts` also clean. No new dependency: the configuration file is TOML and `tomllib` is stdlib in 3.12.

escalations.detail: A new configuration FILE, `config/hosts.toml`, read by `helena.hosts.load`. Recorded because `concept/instruction.md` §3 and `prds/CONTEXT.md` §6 make 'a second store of any kind, including a cache, a queue or a file' an escalation, and this is a file. Judged not to be a store and built anyway, for two reasons: `concept/04` requires exactly this ('a closed, versioned field set from fixed configuration only'), so refusing to read a file would leave the task unimplementable; and nothing is ever written to it, nothing durable is recovered from it, and it holds no evidence — it is deployment input of the same kind as `.env`, read once at startup and frozen. If the operator disagrees, the file is the only thing to move and `load(path)` already takes the path.

deferred: Every host attribute an asset inventory usually has — owner, location, business criticality, operating system, asset tag. `concept/04` names two fields and no note in this repository names a third, so adding one would be inventing a requirement (`concept/instruction.md` §4). It is the more expensive invention in this particular place: the set is CLOSED, so a field nobody populates renders as `unknown` on every host in every rendering, spending the triage budget on a column of nothing. A field arrives with the increment that has something populating it and something reading it, and it arrives as `v2`.

A closed vocabulary for `device_type`. `concept/04` says 'device type' and gives no list. Closing it over a guessed set (server / workstation / printer / camera) would be the same invention one level down, and an operator whose fleet has a kind the list forgot would have to record something false. It is bounded, single-line, operator-supplied text; nothing joins on it. If evaluation shows triage reasons better against a closed vocabulary, that is a measurement and then a `v2`.

Wrapping the host section into a `helena.contracts.v1.RenderedSection`. `hosts.render` returns the BODY, and the package imports no contract version at all — which is deliberate twice over: it is what makes the import test above a complete answer, and it stops a contract `v2` from reaching back into the attribute set. `tests/test_hosts.py` builds the `RenderedSection` to show the two fit; task 28 is what does it in the code.

The rendering version. This task versions the ATTRIBUTE SET, which is a different dimension: a `rendering_version` bumped for the TLS parameter subset must not read as a change to what the host section's fields mean. `VersionSet.rendering_version` stays task 28/29's.

Storing anything. No assessment table exists yet (task 26 deferred it to D5), so the attribute set version is recorded on a rendering in memory and has not yet been written onto a citable row. `concept/instruction.md` §7's 'versions recorded on every citable row' stays open for the agent layer, exactly as task 26 left it.

A second copy of the attribute set version in SQL. There is none — nothing in the engine reads the host attributes, by construction — so there is no pair of constants to assert equal, unlike `AGGREGATION_VERSION`.
lessons: `concept/04`'s 'fixed configuration only' is testable, but not by feeding something a bad value: what must not exist is a code path. The three tests that work are (1) an allow-list of the package's imports read off the AST, (2) an AST scan of the rest of `src/helena` for anything naming the types or the private functions that mint a host attribute — note that `ast.Name` alone MISSES `from helena.hosts import HostAttributes`, you need `ast.alias` too, which a mutation check caught, and (3) a behavioural test with a real claim about the host in a real engine. Keeping the package free of every `helena` import is what makes (1) a complete answer rather than a blocklist somebody has to keep current.

The evidence table `helena_reference_enrichment_evidence` from migration 0011 IS NOT THERE: 0014 drops it and derives the evidence shape as the view `helena_reference_evidence` over `helena_reference_threatfox`. A test that inserts evidence inserts a feed row into the ThreatFox table and reads the view. `tests/test_view_layering.py`'s `retired` map is the place that records this; the 0011 file still reads as if its table were live.

A configured attribute value is operator text that ends up on its own line of a model prompt, so it is bounded and refused if it carries a newline: `device_type = "laptop\naddress: 198.51.100.4"` would otherwise forge a second attribute line in the body. The same reasoning applies to any later section built as `key: value` lines.

`unknown` is deliberately the same word as the taxonomy's `unknown` root, because `concept/04` spells it that way and inventing a second spelling would be inventing vocabulary. They never meet — one is a verdict in a result, the other a value in the host section of a rendering — but the collision is worth knowing about before someone greps for it.

The committed `config/hosts.toml` entry is the flow fixture's own host, `10.127.0.100`, and its `device_type` is read off `data/ingest/README.md` ('one Windows 10 endpoint', 'a managed enterprise endpoint') rather than made up. A test asserts the configured address is the one address the fixture actually carries, so the two cannot drift.
failed_approaches: Having `helena.hosts` import `helena.contracts.v1` and return a finished `RenderedSection`. Written that way first and backed out before it was committed: it would have coupled the attribute set to a contract version (a contract `v2` would silently change what the host section object is), and it would have gutted the import test, which is the strongest evidence this task has that no agent output can reach a host attribute. Returning the body as text costs task 28 one line.
next_session_should_know: Part one of the five-part rendering is done and the other four are yours. Call `hosts.load()` once (it is frozen and read-once — there is no reload, because a set of host attributes that changed under a running triage stage would make two assessments of the same host incomparable for a reason neither records), then `configuration.attributes_for(address)` per host, then `hosts.render(attributes)` for the body. Wrap it as `RenderedSection(section=contract.HOST, body=..., evidence_ids=(), truncation=None)`: `evidence_ids` is empty ON PURPOSE — `concept/04` requires a stable evidence identifier on every ENRICHED value, and a configured attribute is not one, so a citation here would point at configuration as though a source had claimed it. There is nothing to truncate either; the host section is the one part whose size does not depend on what the host did, so the budget you are sizing in task 29 can treat it as a constant. Two things not to break. (1) The body's first line is `attribute_set_version: v1` and that is where the attribute set version lives, because `RenderedSection` is frozen and has no field for it — do not move it into `Rendering.version`, which is the rendering's own version and a different dimension. (2) `helena/hosts/` imports NOTHING else in `helena`, and `tests/test_hosts.py::test_the_package_imports_nothing_that_could_reach_an_agent_or_the_store` will fail if you add one; if your renderer needs something from the hosts package, import the hosts package into the renderer, never the reverse. Also: `helena_reference_enrichment_evidence` does not exist — 0014 dropped it and `helena_reference_evidence` is the view; if you are writing a test that needs evidence in the store, insert into `helena_reference_threatfox` and read the view.
